text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.
- New tax rules have resulted in considerable losses for the Norwegian state. According to a partner at law firm Deloitte & Touche, Norway is becoming a tax paradise for industry.

- Development of the Visund oilfield will cost about nine billion crowns, 800 million crowns more than first expected. Operator Norsk Hydro says it still looks at the project as a breakthrough in cost-saving developments.
- Experts believe SAS could disappear at as an airliner in five to ten years because it refuses to adjust to new deregulations and increased competition.
- A new prognosis from the Central Bank shows a decline in inflation from 2.5 percent this year to two percent in 1998.

- Prime Minister Torbjoern Jagland faces declining support for his Labour party. According to a recent opinion poll, the Labour Party will loose 13 seats in parliament after the elections in September.
- American computer giant Corechange will set up a unit in Norway by August.
